observations.statement: Base64 decoder takes ECX destination, EDX source and plain RET. It scans byte-table values until >=64, decodes groups and residual sextets, writes a terminating NUL at the output cursor. It has no length/capacity parameter or explicit invalid-input rejection. Canonical input alphabet/padding mapping verified from all256 actual table bytes.

Actual15-byte dispatcher MOV ECX1, MOVSD XMM5[EBA8], JMP CADC. Same recovered CADC core param1=1 uses signed64 domain and returns finite truncation toward zero; this selects the correct seed conversion rather than CAC0 unsigned stream conversion.

Full original seed path and interleave confirmed: nonnegative i0..7→SSE double plus0→multiply0.1→add106→native _libm_sse2_tan_precise→absolute mask→multiply100→CAB1 signed64→AL. These seed bytes occupy assembled key even positions; decoded first8 occupy odd positions.

V2 inverse uses derived words1 key then words2 key, then Base64-decodes the inner text. Forward input order is originala45a(V1 Base64 ASCII,words2), then originala45a(result,words1), then marker at offset0 and canonical Base64. Marker search is strstr but actual payload offset remains decoded+18.

Ord9 releases only native factory KeyDec: passes this ECX/flag1 through vtable+4; destructor frees native+4 then sized delete12, RET4. Original derived keys use matching target CRT free IAT. Python buffers are never passed to native free.

derived_decoder_length: For nonnegative small scanned sextet count n, return reduces to floor(3*n/4). Count mod4=1 produces no residual byte and no strict canonical rejection. Valid canonical input only is planned; this inference is not a runtime malformed-input oracle.
